text:
The fault is most likely in **M7**, the diode-connected PMOS pull-up on the output. Its width of 4.039 µm is too large relative to the pull-down M8 (2.02 µm). Because M7 is a diode-connected load from VDD to vout, its strength sets the low-level output: vout_min rises to 0.2248 V, well above the 0.1008 V limit. The same oversized device conducts a large static current when the output is low, which accounts for the ~505 µW average power.

The sensitivities support this. Increasing M7 raises both failing metrics (+16.9% on vout_min_rel, +11.6% on power), and increasing M8 pulls vout_min down (-14.5%). The hysteresis and high-level specs pass, and the input-stage devices (M2, M4) barely affect vout_min, so the fault is in the output stage.
